metadata.title: LunarLab: software, study records and trained policies for auditable reward-design experiments
metadata.description:
Software and research data for LunarLab, a toolkit for auditable reward-design experiments in reinforcement learning, prepared for a software article (manuscript in preparation).

  • source/: the LunarLab repository at revision c0d9e5d0823167584a7bff37de9661c35a58228c (see REVISIONS.md): the library whose code is that of revision c9b9384, tests, documentation, protocols, study records, the audit-workflow comparison programs and fixtures, the package validator and results;
  • software/: deterministic, installable source archives;
  • lunarlander-study/: the historical 38-policy LunarLander export (3,800 recorded test episodes; the six learned-reward packages with their original reward models) and its repair-time source archive;
  • cartpole-study-output/: the CartPole study's 36 frozen checkpoints and 18 exported audit artifacts, and an inventory of the 156 scheduled checkpoints that are not distributed;
  • outside-git/: the 14 policies of the comparison fixtures.

START_HERE.md explains how to check the archive from a fresh extraction with the included validator, which installs locked dependencies into a new environment and uses an empty data home. Nothing is trained.

Limitations: on Windows, the recording platform, all 38 LunarLander policies replay exactly from a fresh extraction. On Linux, nine policies were replayed in CI, and an assistant-executed audit replayed all 38 in a diagnostic run whose parent validation was interrupted: all kept integrity, 37 showed permitted numerical differences, and one DQN policy disagreed significantly with its recorded mean return (224.07 recorded, 230.45 on Linux); its cause is not identified. Bit-identical results across operating systems are not a supported guarantee. The LunarLander policies were trained from a modified working tree based on revision 32823f3, as their records state; that tree is not reconstructed. No independent person has yet used LunarLab.
